translation:
(The above sets forth the root of the disease; it is the first half of this section. Below, the meaning of the classics is cited in full, to verify its truth and complete its principle.)

As for what is called thirst from reversal of the qi of the heart and lung, the Jue Lun (厥論) says: When the heart shifts its heat to the lung, it is transmitted and becomes diaphragm wasting (膈消). The commentary says: When heart-heat enters the lung, and after a long time is transmitted and transformed, internally it becomes diaphragm heat, with wasting-thirst and much drinking. As for what is called thirst from liver bi (肝痹), the Bi Lun (痹論) says: In liver bi, when one lies down at night one is startled, drinks much, and urinates frequently.
translator_notes: 膈消 rendered 'diaphragm wasting'; 痹 kept as 'bi' with original character; 厥論/痹論 kept as chapter names.
